content.text:
Fixed.

**`fastify.js:395`** — tightened the `closeAllConnections()` branch to `forceCloseConnections === true`. Since #6669 narrowed the first branch to `serverFactory`, the string `'idle'` fell through to this loose truthiness check on native servers and force-destroyed in-flight sockets. Native servers with `'idle'` now call neither method and rely on `server.close()`, which closes idle connections on its own (Node ≥19). The `serverFactory` path, `forceCloseConnections: true`, and the `kKeepAliveConnections` reap loop are untouched.

**`test/close.test.js`** — two tests covering an in-flight request (400ms handler, `close()` at 100ms) with explicit `forceCloseConnections: 'idle'` and with default options. Verified both fail on the unpatched code with `UND_ERR_SOCKET` and pass with the fix; the full file is 24/24 passing.

One note on the tests: each closes its undici client before awaiting `close()`. Without that, the run takes ~70s per test — the server's `close()` had already passed its idle sweep by the time the response was read, so the now-idle keep-alive socket lingers until a timeout. That's a property of `server.close()` semantics rather than anything introduced here, but it does mean an `'idle'` shutdown does not proactively reap a connection that becomes idle after `close()` was called. Worth a follow-up look if that matters; I left it alone as out of scope.

I did not run eslint — the command needed approval. The added code follows the file's existing style.
